calls.head: Don’t buy Daccord’s record against the Panthers
calls.body: Daccord has been a wall against the Panthers since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Daccord isn’t that wall tonight.
calls.call: If Daccord starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .905 than to his .936 against the Panthers.

calls.head: The Kraken can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Kraken’s penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Panthers’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Kraken tonight.

calls.head: The Panthers lock it down, the Kraken don’t
calls.body: The Panthers keep shots away, but the Kraken give up plenty. Florida is one of the league’s best for shot suppression, and Seattle is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Kraken to give up the bigger pile of shots.

surprises.head: Joey Daccord got lit up
surprises.body: Daccord allowed 8 goals on 37 shots, worth 4.6 expected goals: 3.4 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 60 starts.

story.head: Hat tricks for Bennett and Verhaeghe
paras: It was a busy first period. Sam Bennett got the scoring started for the Panthers just over a minute in, but Shane Wright tied it 1-1 for Seattle less than four minutes later. Carter Verhaeghe scored late in the first and again a little over a minute later to put the Panthers up 3-1. The second was all Panthers: Verhaeghe completed a natural hat trick, Niko Mikkola scored, and Bennett scored his second of the night to make it 6-1. Frédérick Gaudreau cut Florida’s lead to 6-2 late in the second, and Sam Reinhart stretched the lead to 7-2 on the power play early in the third. Ryker Evans made it 7-3 less than two minutes later, far too late to matter. Bennett completed his hat trick midway through the third to make it 8-3 for the Panthers, his 400th NHL point. Matthew Tkachuk finished with three assists.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Panthers win about seven in ten. Jacob Markström made 20 saves for the Cats, and Joey Daccord allowed eight goals on 37 shots. By our Swing measure, Brady Tkachuk had the best night of anyone, even with Bennett’s and Verhaeghe’s hat tricks in the game.
The Panthers killed all four Kraken power plays. The Panthers improved to 5-2-2, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Kraken fell to 5-3-1, third in the Pacific.

items.text: Matthew Tkachuk passed Scott Mellanby for ninth on the Panthers’ all-time assists list, with 198.
Sam Bennett passed Aaron Ekblad for tenth on the Panthers’ all-time goals list, with 124.
Three straight wins for the Panthers.
Mackie Samoskevich played his first game back in Florida.
